claims.text: The proposed initial alloy has a density below 6 g/cm³.
The initial alloy is a non-equilibrium, metastable single-phase solid solution containing Mg and other constituents such as Al, Cu, Zn, and Gd.
The as-cast baseline contains no significant intermetallic precipitation.
Controlled thermal aging at elevated temperature activates Mg diffusion and phase transformation.
During thermal exposure, Mg diffuses out of the metastable matrix and segregates.
Mg segregation produces fine Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
The Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates form both along grain boundaries and within the matrix.
Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates nucleate or catalyze the growth of a protective mixed oxide scale.
The proposed mixed oxide scale contains MgO and potentially Al2O3.
A dense, continuous, and adherent protective oxide scale retards oxygen ingress and slows high-temperature oxidation.
Thermally aged specimens will exhibit lower oxidation mass gain than as-cast specimens.
Thermally aged specimens will exhibit a lower corrosion rate, including lower electrochemical current density, than as-cast specimens.
The predicted oxidation and corrosion improvements are directly caused by oxide-scale development guided by Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
A modest Mg content is sufficient to generate distinct Mg-rich intermetallics during aging.
The mechanism applies only when exposure activates diffusion without causing excessive precipitate coarsening or melting.
Mg-segregation kinetics, oxide composition and continuity, and performance improvements depend on alloy composition, Mg level, aging temperature, and aging time.
